o1.biggest_strength: A full, build-ready flow with exact copy for every reason and outcome. It brings the pause back for "no time" and gives goal-reached people a kind exit with a "remind me" option. The Cancel button is always live, and the maths ties out (842 vs 2,239 kept, about £11.3k a month more).
o1.biggest_mistake: It gives a single point estimate with no honest range. It also leaves the 50% off in place for app-switchers and builds the reminder and annual-switch numbers on the discount's take rate without flagging how shaky that is.
o1.what_would_make_it_a_10: Add a low-to-high range on the untested offers and a plain warning that the flow depends on the pause, and cut the discount for the switching group or justify it with data.

o2.biggest_strength: It leads with the money and the bad news. The pause does 80% of the work, and without it the flow keeps fewer than today. It gives a range (+1,230 to +1,680), names rebuilding the pause as this week's first move, and adds a measurement plan with a threshold.
o2.biggest_mistake: The "goal reached or trip over" screen is a plain exit with no remind-me-later option. The Cancel button is inactive until a reason is picked, and the 12-month revenue figures rest on unexplained churn assumptions.
o2.what_would_make_it_a_10: Add a "remind me before my next trip" option on the trip-over screen, keep the Cancel button live at all times, and show the working behind the 12-month revenue numbers.

reason: Both flows are close on the facts. Output 2 tells me the uncomfortable truth that the whole plan rests on the pause, gives an honest range, and says what to build first and what to watch. Output 1 has slightly kinder copy for trip-over learners and an always-live cancel button, but it feels less candid about risk.
